blocks.content: This is one of the most consistently confused pairs in Docker, and worth nailing down clearly: EXPOSE is documentation baked into the image, -p (publish) is the only thing that actually opens a port to the outside.

As covered in the Dockerfile module, EXPOSE is a line in the Dockerfile documenting which port the application inside is meant to listen on. It has zero effect on actual network reachability, on its own.

blocks.alt: A documentation line, baked into the image

blocks.content: 2. Publish Is What Actually Opens the Door
blocks.text: 2. Publish Is What Actually Opens the Door

blocks.content: Only -p (or -P) at docker run time actually creates a real path from the host into the container's port. This is a runtime decision, made when you start the container, entirely separate from anything declared in the Dockerfile.

blocks.alt: The runtime flag that actually creates reachability

blocks.content: This independence is the part that trips people up: you can -p publish a port the Dockerfile never EXPOSEd at all, and it will work perfectly fine. You can EXPOSE a port and never publish it, and it remains completely unreachable from outside the container.

blocks.alt: Publishing works with or without a matching EXPOSE line

blocks.content:
# This works even though the Dockerfile never had EXPOSE 3000
docker run -p 3000:3000 myapp

# This does nothing for reachability, EXPOSE alone changes nothing
# Dockerfile: EXPOSE 3000
docker run myapp   # port 3000 is still not reachable from the host

blocks.content: The mixup is understandable, EXPOSE sounds like it should expose something to the network. In practice, treat it purely as documentation and as input to -P's auto-publish behavior, and treat -p as the only instruction that actually, meaningfully opens a port.

blocks.alt: Reframing what each one actually controls

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: EXPOSE documents an intended port inside the Dockerfile, it has no effect on actual network reachability by itself.
-p (or -P) at docker run time is the only thing that actually publishes a port, and it works completely independently of whether EXPOSE was ever declared.
